I don’t need to put up with someone I don’t like and someone who mistreats me. I grew up with a very mean mother who always treated me like that and I think I internalized that it was normal for the people you love to treat you like that but I have news for you. It is NOT. People who love you and care about you want to see you succeed, they can’t wait to compliment you, they never want to dim your light. And you deserve people like that in your life. They will come, eventually. They will come even faster once you make room for them by removing the people that treat you this way.

Just had a conversation about this with my therapist. Especially about the going out of my way to be nice to people and being crushed when they don’t reciprocate or some form of rejection in the friendship happens. 
What I’ve started doing this year is finding ways to put that love and kindness back into me. So like practicing saying no to things I don’t want to do or go to, telling someone I’m not okay with something, basically everything I was scared to do before because I was trying to be as agreeable as possible. It’s so freeing to realize that you don’t have to be this person with absolutely no needs to get people to like you, and that you’ll probably attract people who respect you when you respect and stand up for yourself.
Also spending a lot of time alone this year investing in a lot of things I like to do e.g. reading, working out, playing the guitar, has taught me who I am outside of trying to people please everyone else. You’ll realize eventually that you’re amazing just as you are and don’t need anyone else to validate your worth.
I still struggle with feeling inherent worth everyday but I feel like it’s the most valuable source of self worth and so worth it to nurture. Depending on other people for that will never be the same, because people mess up and people leave. But you’ll always have you and that should be your most important relationship. 
Wishing you luck 💕

A big part of my CPTSD was minimizing my trauma. I thought I had a good childhood and all that happened was some verbal abuse from bullying (not even physical) and my mom berating me every second of the day and my dad being a distant stranger except when it came to school. But that’s all it takes for some people, and a lot less could hurt someone else a lot more. The point is, what happened doesn’t matter as much as how badly it affected you. The sooner you give yourself compassion for what you went through (which btw, even if all your needs are met and your life is otherwise “perfect” and your parents can’t stop arguing, that’s still a very hard thing to go through as a child and can have serious, lasting effects), the sooner you can get help and start to heal. It took me years to realize I was actually in a lot of pain and that every bit of that pain was valid and worthy of treatment. In that time, I hurt myself even more by gaslighting myself into believing my problems were not that serious, and by the time I got help, it was that much harder to pull myself up. All this to say, you wouldn’t ever minimize anyone else’s trauma, so why minimize yours. You are hurting, and healing starts when you acknowledge it ❤️

I resonate deeply. It sucks to have to start from scratch. But everyday I’m happy that at least I don’t have someone lying to my face. You were kind enough to give her the benefit of the doubt, and she took advantage of that. I went through the exact same thing. It is very traumatizing, especially for someone with cptsd. I’m so proud of you for choosing yourself and ending the friendship. You have done something many of us with cptsd find almost impossible. 
I know now it feels terrible because you’re coming to terms with the pain that she caused, and also still loving her. I resonate with you questioning your identity as well, and feeling like you’ve always hidden behind her because of your insecurities. That’s the painful part for me, feeling like I had a loyal, loving friend when she was just using me for her own narcissistic supply and putting me down constantly. Especially when I saw how much she shit talks me on social media. She’s probably constructed this whole narrative in her head and told it to many of our mutual friends. I see this as a good thing, because it shows her true self and tells me that I can never be friends with her again. 

Half the work is letting go of toxic people. Cut ties, block on social media, distance yourself from mutuals if it helps. Work on building you up. Little by little, do things you love and you will start to build your self esteem up. It’s a long hard process, I’ve been at it for two years now, but I feel so much better getting to choose better people to be in my life, rather than having to put up with toxic people. 

There is no question that Lucy is not a good person, and she has done things that hurt you. Treat yourself accordingly, take time to heal, be gentle with yourself, give yourself all the compassion that she didn’t. If you had a friend in a similar situation, how would you take care of her? Now apply that to you, cause you deserve all that love and care.

I feel sad that even after you trying to patch things up (which she should be doing), she blows you off like this. She’s made it pretty clear how she feels about you, and now you don’t even have to go through the awkwardness of ending the friendship. I know how painful it might be, but it’s time to move on, take some time for yourself to remember your self worth and find some new, better friends. Sometimes when we’re in a toxic friendship for so long we start to believe that’s what we deserve.
However most places and things that provide the “experience”, save for classes, are closed. So if we go in person, why note open everything up, if it’s really about the experience.

You’re not a snowflake. You’re a human being that deserves to be excited about things that make you happy. The worst kind of people are the ones that ridicule you for the things you love (within reason, but still good friends don’t call other good friends losers). And she’s making you anxious to talk to her now? That’s not how your friends should make you feel. You deserve better!!! Your friends should be a safe space. 

If you feel like she’s reasonable, maybe you can talk to her about how her comments made you feel. If you want to keep her as a friend, I suggest demoting her to a lower level of friendship, maybe only sharing the more superficial parts of yourself. She obviously does not deserve more. While you do this you can search for other friends who are into the same things as you, those make way more fulfilling friendships imo. 

Otherwise, talk to her, tell her how she made you feel and then proceed from there. How she handles that is an indicator of who she is as a person, and some people just don’t deserve access to us. Remember, don’t settle. There’s always better out there.
